requirements.requirement: Run a web application on node1 that serves successfully on port 8080.
requirements.summary: The application listened on port 8080 and returned HTTP 200 with a healthy response both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Run the application inside a chroot as the unprivileged appsvc account.
requirements.summary: Direct process inspection showed UID 105/GID 499 and a process root of /srv/app-chroot. The appsvc account was locked and configured with /bin/false, while the HTTP response independently reported UID 105 and the chroot-only identity file.

requirements.requirement: Start the application automatically at boot without requiring an interactive login session.
requirements.summary: SysV runlevel links were installed, and a bounded reboot demonstrated automatic recovery in runlevel 2. After reboot the service had PPID 1, remained healthy, and no interactive sessions were present. The restart protocol captured the healthy baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, persistent file hashes, and recovered service state; the fixed lifecycle boot identities corroborate the transition.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic. The deployed application used the installed Python 2.5.1 runtime and functioned successfully before and after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence, including a complete node1 reboot-and-recovery transition. The application runs in the requested chroot under the locked appsvc identity, serves healthy HTTP responses on port 8080, starts without a login session, and preserves the legacy operating system and kernel.
limitations: The lifecycle listening-socket snapshot was empty after execution despite repeated direct ss and HTTP observations showing the service on port 8080; the captured data does not explain this collector discrepancy.
Systemd failed-service inspection was unsupported on this SysV-era platform, so absence of unrelated failed services could not be independently established through that lifecycle probe.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account/chroot creation, application and init-script installation, startup registration, and reboot were directly connected to the required outcomes. The failed initial setup command stopped at unsupported groupadd -r before evidence of a mutation (cmd-c1f36ef0d0994508); the failed first service start was followed by the necessary init-script correction (cmd-6640def07f164cdd, cmd-8ece0dc038164f68). The transient reboot log left no final /tmp residue. Package health remained clean, the platform was retained, and no unrelated final changes were captured.
